result.topic_en: Euler explains that the first part of the variation vanishes when the Euler–Lagrange-type equation holds (giving the maximum or minimum curve), and begins explaining the second part of the variation, which refers to the endpoints M and A.
result.transcription:
58 METHODVS NOVA CALCVLVM

38. Haec igitur prima pars variationis inuoluit omnia ſpatiola Y $v$ intra terminos A et M contenta, quae quum in infinitum variari poſſint, atque adeo a poſitiuis ad negatiua tranſire queant, maximae variationes hic locum habere poſſunt. Verum tamen vnicus caſus hinc debet excipi, quo curva A M ita eſt comparata, vt ſit
$0 = N - \frac{dP}{dx} + \frac{ddQ}{dx^2} - \frac{d^3R}{dx^3} + \frac{d^4S}{dx^4}$ etc.
tum enim vtcunque curuae proximae fuerint comparatae, iſta pars prima variationis, ſemper in nihilum abit. Neque deuiatio curuarum proximarum $\alpha\mu$ a principali A M intra terminos A et M quicquam ad variationem confert; ex quo haec curua reſpectu formulae integralis $\int Z\,dx$ inprimis eſt memorabilis, quandoquidem in ea haec formula integralis vel maximum vel minimum obtinet valorem.

Explicatio partis ſecundae in variatione.
39. Progrediamur nunc ad ſecundam partem variationis ſupra inuentae, quae eſt
$dt\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)\left(P - \frac{dQ}{dx} + \frac{ddR}{dx^2} - \frac{d^3S}{dx^3} + \text{etc.}\right)$
circa quam primum obſeruo, quoniam ea ad terminum M refertur per integrationem rite inſtitutam, inſuper adiici debere, ſimilem expreſſionem ad terminum priorem A relatam, at vero ſigno contrario affectam, id quod ideo eſt neceſſarium vt facto $x = 0$, etiam haec expreſſio penitus tollatur. Refertur autem iſta pars
$dt\left(\frac{dy}{dt}\right)\left(P - \frac{dQ}{dx} + \frac{ddR}{dx^2} - \text{etc.}\right)$

vnice

items.quote: tum enim vtcunque curuae proximae fuerint comparatae, iſta pars prima variationis, ſemper in nihilum abit.
items.english: For then, however the neighbouring curves are constituted, this first part of the variation always vanishes.

items.quote: ex quo haec curua reſpectu formulae integralis $\int Z\,dx$ inprimis eſt memorabilis, quandoquidem in ea haec formula integralis vel maximum vel minimum obtinet valorem.
items.english: Hence this curve is especially remarkable with respect to the integral formula ∫Z dx, since on it this integral formula attains either a maximum or a minimum value.

items.quote: inſuper adiici debere, ſimilem expreſſionem ad terminum priorem A relatam, at vero ſigno contrario affectam, id quod ideo eſt neceſſarium vt facto $x = 0$, etiam haec expreſſio penitus tollatur.
items.english: Moreover a similar expression referred to the earlier endpoint A, but with the opposite sign, must be added; this is necessary so that, on setting x = 0, this expression also vanishes completely.
